title: Coordinated cross-region traffic drain with tenant-priority and emergency hotpatch
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: This ticket captures the runbook and emergency fix path for coordinated cross-region traffic drains when a regional service regression affects latency or correctness. Scope covers Hosted API routing, Dedicated tenant pools, and Private (VPC) deployments when partner-managed control planes request guidance. The focus is to: 1) safely evacuate traffic from a degraded region with tenant-prioritization (SLA customers first), 2) preserve KV-cache/LLM context warmup to reduce error/regression risk, and 3) ship an emergency kernel-scheduling hotpatch for a race we observed that amplifies cross-region desynchronization under heavy tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook tested in staging with simulated region outage and verified tenant-priority ordering works (SLA-marked tenants drained first)
Automated traffic-shift automation triggers with expected fallback model variants and verifies per-tenant tokenization compatibility
Emergency hotpatch (kernel scheduler tweak) passes canary in two regions with no regression for p99 latency over 72h
Post-incident checklist completed and communicated to affected customers within SLA window
mitigation_plan: Immediate: Set routing policy for affected region to 'drain' with max 30s connection TTL and disable new long-running streams
Priority drain: Mark tenants with 'SLA=enterprise' and drain them to dedicated spare capacity or alternate region first
Cache preservation: For requests with session_id, preserve KV cache snapshot and prefer sticky routing to warmed hosts in target region when possible
Fallback models: Route to smaller-quantized compatible model variants (e.g., model-v2-q4_0) for best-effort continuity if top-tier variant unavailable
Communication: Open incident bridge, notify SRE/PM/Support with templated customer messages and per-tenant escalation list
short_term_hotpatch_steps: Branch runtime-hotfix/kernel-sched-fix, run unit and smoke tests against nightly image
Canary deploy hotpatch to a single AZ in an alternate region with traffic shadowing from degraded region
Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and KV miss rate for 3 hours, rollback if error rate increases > 2x
If canary stable, roll to all non-affected regions in waves (25% -> 50% -> 100%) using the console rollout tool
After full roll, coordinate final drain of bad region and validate no request replay/desync
rollback_plan: If hotpatch causes regressions, immediately run console rollback to previous runtime image on newly patched hosts
Re-open expired connections only after verifying KV consistency between regions
If rollback is unavailable due to infra state, engage infra-ops to provision temporary spare nodes in an alternative region and move SLA tenants
Document root cause and required follow-ups in postmortem before reattempting patch
long_term_action_items: Add tenant-priority routing as a first-class config in the control plane with safe defaults and testing harness
Improve KV cache replication semantics to allow 'read-only warm handoff' between regions during drains
Automate staged hotpatch promotion with integrated canary metrics (SLO gates) to reduce manual risk
Add dedicated capacity reservation APIs for emergency tenant relocation to speed SLA handling
Formalize Private deployment coordination checklist for customer-managed upgrades and emergency traffic shifts
steps_to_execute_on_incident: 1) Pager escalates to SRE and ENG leads; open bridge with links to dashboards
2) Shift region to 'drain' mode and set connection TTL to 30s
3) Apply tenant-priority policy: move SLA tenants first using console 'evacuate' command
4) Shadow traffic to canary hotpatch if available and monitor for regressions
5) If degraded region cannot recover in 15 minutes, enable fallback route to quantized model variants and notify customers
6) After successful eviction, mark region 'quiesced' and begin controlled reboot/maintenance
